page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the arm64 CPU architecture. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs alongside 256.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of RAM allocated per core. The instance operates without integrated hardware accelerators, providing zero GPUs, and relies entirely on external network-attached block storage as it contains no bundled local storage disks.

The 64 dedicated arm64 cores deliver concurrent multi-threaded execution capacity suited for parallel processing tasks. Because the instance provisions a standard memory footprint without dedicated local NVMe drives, storage I/O performance is contingent on the attached persistent block storage configuration chosen at deployment. In addition, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default, requiring network routing or external IP provisioning via Google Cloud VPC services.

In terms of qualitative efficiency, the arm64 design offers a resource-dense configuration for large-scale production services that benefit from high concurrency at standardized resource ratios. The configuration avoids the overhead of specialized GPU or high-speed local disk hardware, keeping infrastructure allocation focused strictly on memory and compute capacity.

Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-64 is well suited for container orchestration nodes, microservices clusters, enterprise web applications, intermediate data pipelines, build infrastructure, and scale-out multi-tier application backends requiring substantial core counts on an ARM architecture.
